At the moment of hatching, the neonates emerge at an initial wet weight of just 1.55 grams [Ww0 = 1.55 grams]. This modest mass places them among the lighter hatchlings in the genus Sporophila, a pattern likely linked to the species' reliance on a diet of grass seeds, which provides a reliable but not exceptionally nutrient-dense resource for provisioning parents. Once hatched, the nestling chick enters a phase of rapid somatic growth that is heavily dependent on consistent parental provisioning. The altricial nestling, initially weighing just over one and a half grams, must therefore increase its body mass more than sevenfold before it can achieve independence. The parents, working in tandem, deliver a steady supply of partially digested seeds, which fuels this extraordinary growth trajectory.
